items.action: On every `<ds-split-button>` whose `menuItems` can be empty, pass the items or replace the control with `<ds-button>`.
items.appliesWhen: Only a `<ds-split-button>` that renders with `menuItems` empty — a list filled after the first render, a list built by a filter that can return nothing, or a split button used for one action. A split button whose items are always present behaves exactly as before.
items.pitfall: Nothing errors and the main button keeps working, so this is only visible on the chevron: it is disabled while the list is empty. Items fetched after the first render therefore leave a disabled chevron for as long as the fetch takes, which reads as a broken control to anyone who does not know it is waiting. Render the split button once the items are in hand, or keep the interval deliberately.
items.note: The chevron previously opened a `ds-menu` with nothing in it. It is now disabled while `menuItems` is empty and enables itself when items arrive — disabled rather than hidden, so the control keeps its geometry either way. A development build warns and names `ds-button` as the control for a single action. The panel can only ever be the `ds-menu` built from `menuItems`; anything else composes from `ds-button` and `ds-popover`.
items.verify: A split button with an empty `menuItems` shows a disabled chevron and opens no panel, and one with items opens its menu as before.

items.action: If you set `--focus-ring-inner` to a colour to get a visible ring back, remove that override — it no longer reaches a control's ring. To restyle the ring, set `--focus-ring-width`, `--focus-ring-color` or `--focus-ring-offset`.
items.appliesWhen: Every focusable control in the library — buttons, checkboxes, radios, switches, tabs, menu rows, list rows, segments, days, links. Fields keep their soft halo and are unaffected; `--focus-ring-inner` still composes the halo that `data-focus="ring"` opts into.
items.pitfall: An `outline: none` in your own stylesheet now removes a control's indicator outright, where before it removed nothing because the ring was a shadow. Any reset that zeroes outlines on DS controls leaves a keyboard user with no indicator, and nothing errors.
items.note: Controls draw the ring with `outline` + `outline-offset` instead of a two-layer box-shadow. `outline-offset` leaves its gap UNPAINTED, so the gap shows whatever the control actually sits on; the shadow gap had to be filled with a guessed colour, which was a coloured rim wherever the guess was wrong. A negative offset draws the ring inside the element, so a clipping ancestor can no longer eat it. Components no longer touch `box-shadow` on focus, so a focused card keeps its elevation and a selected segment keeps its shadow.
items.verify: Focus a button standing on a tinted band: the gap shows the band, not a surface-coloured rim. Focus a menu row: the ring is drawn inside the row and is not clipped.

items.action: Replace every `--ds-<component>-focus-shadow` override on a control with `--focus-ring-color`, `--focus-ring-width` or `--focus-ring-offset` on the same scope.
items.appliesWhen: Only the thirteen control components that published one: button, icon-button, card, checkbox, radio, switch, tabs, toast, breadcrumbs, pagination, sidenav-item, sidenav-group, menu-item. Field tokens such as `--ds-input-focus-shadow` are unchanged.
items.pitfall: An override of a removed token is a custom property like any other — it sets, it cascades, and it changes nothing. The control keeps the default ring and no build or console says why.
items.note: Each of these resolved to `--ds-control-focus-shadow`, which controls no longer read. The three ring tokens replace them and cascade the same way, so a per-component override becomes a scoped one: set them on the component's own selector rather than at `:root`.
items.verify: Focus the component you overrode: the ring shows your colour and thickness, not the default brand ring.

items.action: Remove `data-focus="field"` and `data-focus="outline"` from `<html>`. For a tighter ring use `data-focus="edge"`; for a thicker or recoloured one set `--focus-ring-width` and `--focus-ring-color`.
items.appliesWhen: Only an app that sets one of those two values. `ring`, `edge` and `inset` are unchanged and keep their meaning.
items.pitfall: An unknown `data-focus` value matches nothing and is silently ignored, so the app keeps the default indicator and looks merely un-themed rather than misconfigured.
items.note: Both values described a swap of one box-shadow for another. `field` gave controls the halo and `outline` blanked both roles so a single global rule could draw an outline — neither survives now that controls draw their own outline and never a shadow. The ring tokens express what those modes were reaching for, per scope rather than only at the root.
items.verify: Focus a button with the attribute removed: the ring is the default brand outline held off the control.

items.action: Build after upgrading, then rename or mark `override` any member the compiler reports as colliding.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class that extends MenuComponent or RadioComponent. Template users need nothing; `deselectable` is a new input and nothing existing changed name or type.
items.pitfall: Two of the three new members are not public API, which is no protection: a redeclared private or protected member fails with TS2415 exactly as a public collision does. And an `override anyIcon` or `override onClick` written before this release compiles clean while overriding nothing.
items.note: MenuComponent gained `anyIcon`, a computed over its content children that decides whether every row reserves the icon slot. RadioComponent gained `deselectable` (a new input) and `onClick`.
items.verify: The app builds with no TS4114 / TS2415 / TS2416 naming MenuComponent or RadioComponent, and no override of anyIcon, deselectable or onClick remains in your source.

items.action: If you positioned anything against a checkbox, radio or switch focus ring, re-measure it against the row rather than the glyph.
items.appliesWhen: Only `ds-checkbox`, `ds-radio` and `ds-switch`. `ds-table`'s cell checkbox is unchanged — it has no label row, so it keeps ringing its own box.
items.pitfall: Nothing errors and the control still rings, so this shows up only as a ring that is wider than it was and starts at the label's far edge. A layout that reserved space for a 24px ring around a 20px glyph now has a ring as wide as the label.
items.note: Ringing the glyph drew a brand ring concentric with the brand ring the checked state already paints, which reads as a target rather than as two states a keyboard user must tell apart while moving through a group. The row is what the pointer already hits, because the label carries the hit area. A control with no label collapses back onto the glyph, and there the ring stands further off instead.
items.verify: Tab to a checked radio: the ring surrounds glyph and label together, and is not concentric with the dot.

informational: The focus ring now eases its colour in over `--duration-fast`, as a CSS animation rather than a transition so a component's own transition list is untouched. Geometry does not animate, so nothing moves and no layout shifts. `--duration-fast` is already 0ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, so there is nothing to opt out of.

`ds-multi-select`'s panel search field had no focus indicator — it zeroed its own outline and nothing above it painted one. The row around it rings now, drawn inward because the panel clips. Nothing to change on your side.

Three fields whose only focus indicator was a 1px border tint now draw the standard ring: `ds-sidenav-footer`'s search box, and `ds-table`'s column filter and inline cell editor. Nothing to change on your side.

A ds-date-picker day outside the allowed range no longer highlights under the pointer. The day button is only aria-disabled and never natively disabled, so its hover rule matched a date that could not be picked; hover skips a disabled day now, and the colour and cursor it already carried are unchanged. NO ACTION.

Every hand-written `outline: none` in the library is now `focus.own-indicator`, which skips the suppression under forced colours. Silencing a DS control in your own stylesheet should be wrapped the same way: `@media not (forced-colors: active)`.

A ds-table selection column draws the design system checkbox instead of the browser default, and answers the same hooks as ds-checkbox: --ds-checkbox-bg-color, --ds-checkbox-border-color, --ds-checkbox-hover-border-color, --ds-checkbox-selected-bg-color, --ds-checkbox-selected-border-color and --ds-checkbox-radius reach a table where they previously did nothing. Setting one to restyle your checkboxes now also restyles table row selection, which is the intent. The element is still an input[type="checkbox"], so a selector of your own aimed at it still matches; it now competes with the library rule rather than styling something nothing else touched, and the box sets appearance: none. NO ACTION unless that override is what you were relying on.

Text under .t-mono no longer ligates: the face draws === as one triple-bar glyph and != as a struck equals, so prose naming an operator showed something other than the characters it discussed. Set --ds-t-mono-ligatures to normal to get them back. The change is visual and applies wherever .t-mono is used; nothing about the class, the font size or the weight moved. NO ACTION.
